title: Euclid's Constructions
blurb: Sixteen classic compass-and-straightedge problems, from the equilateral triangle to the regular pentagon.

items.title: Equilateral Triangle
items.subtitle: Euclid I.1
items.text:
Construct a point $C$ so that triangle $ABC$ is equilateral, with $A$, $B$ and $C$ going counterclockwise.

::: Hint
Every point on the circle centered at $A$ through $B$ is exactly $AB$ away from $A$.
:::

items.title: Perpendicular Bisector
items.text:
Construct the line that crosses segment $AB$ at right angles through its midpoint.

::: Hint
Every point on that line is the same distance from $A$ as from $B$.
:::

items.title: Midpoint
items.subtitle: Euclid I.10
items.text:
Construct the midpoint of segment $AB$.

::: Hint
The perpendicular bisector crosses $AB$ at the midpoint.
:::

items.title: Perpendicular Through a Point
items.subtitle: Euclid I.11–12
items.text:
Construct the line through $P$ at right angles to $\ell$.

::: Hint
A circle centered at $P$ crosses $\ell$ at two points that are the same distance from $P$.
:::

items.title: Mirror Image
items.text:
Reflect point $P$ across line $\ell$.

::: Hint
The reflection lies on the perpendicular to $\ell$ through $P$, as far from $\ell$ as $P$ is.
:::

items.title: Parallel Line
items.subtitle: Euclid I.31
items.text:
Construct the line through $P$ parallel to $\ell$.

::: Hint
Opposite sides of a rhombus are parallel, and all four of its sides use one compass setting.
:::

items.title: Angle Bisector
items.subtitle: Euclid I.9
items.text:
Construct the line that bisects the acute angle between $\ell$ and $m$.

::: Hint
Mark off equal distances along both lines from the point where they cross.
:::

items.title: Transfer a Distance
items.subtitle: Euclid I.2
items.text:
Construct the circle centered at $C$ with radius $AB$. The compass collapses when lifted, so the distance can't be carried over directly.

::: Hint
Reflect $B$ across the perpendicular bisector of $AC$.
:::

items.title: Trisect a Segment
items.subtitle: Euclid VI.9
items.text:
Construct the two points that divide $AB$ into three equal parts.

::: Hint
In any triangle, the medians cross one third of the way along each one.
:::

items.title: Circle Through Three Points
items.subtitle: Euclid IV.5
items.text:
Construct the circle that passes through $A$, $B$ and $C$.

::: Hint
Its center is the same distance from all three points.
:::

items.title: Find the Center
items.subtitle: Euclid III.1
items.text:
Construct the center of circle $\omega$.

::: Hint
The perpendicular bisector of any chord passes through the center. Use the Point tool to put points on $\omega$.
:::

items.title: Tangents From a Point
items.subtitle: Euclid III.17
items.text:
Construct both lines through $P$ that touch circle $\omega$, which is centered at $O$.

::: Hint
The radius to the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent, so that point sees segment $OP$ at a right angle.
:::

items.title: Regular Hexagon
items.subtitle: Euclid IV.15
items.text:
Inscribe a regular hexagon in circle $\omega$, which is centered at $O$, with a vertex at $A$. Construct the other five vertices.

::: Hint
A regular hexagon's side equals the radius of its circle.
:::

items.title: Square in a Circle
items.subtitle: Euclid IV.6
items.text:
Inscribe a square in circle $\omega$, which is centered at $O$, with a vertex at $A$. Construct the other three vertices.

::: Hint
The diagonals of a square are perpendicular diameters.
:::

items.title: Square on a Segment
items.subtitle: Euclid I.46
items.text:
Construct points $C$ and $D$ so that $ABCD$ is a square, with its corners going counterclockwise.

::: Hint
Raise a perpendicular at $B$ and mark off the length $BA$ along it.
:::

items.title: Regular Pentagon
items.subtitle: Euclid IV.11
items.text:
Inscribe a regular pentagon in circle $\omega$, which is centered at $O$, with a vertex at $A$. Construct the other four vertices.

::: Hint
Draw the diameter perpendicular to $OA$ and find the midpoint $M$ of one of its radii. The circle centered at $M$ through $A$ cuts that diameter at a point whose distance from $A$ is the pentagon's side.
:::
